reply_delivery: Deliver the complete scene in your reply, not in a file. The whole final reply must be {lo}-{hi} words. No title is needed.
file_delivery: Save the complete revised scene in drafts/scene.md, using {lo}-{hi} words. A reply saying it is saved is not a substitute for the file. Change no other project files. Keep the last sentence of the starting draft exactly as written; it is the protected line.
alternatives_delivery: Save three developed directions separately to plans/direction-a.md, plans/direction-b.md, and plans/direction-c.md. Each file must contain {lo}-{hi} words, including any headings. Each needs a specific scene, a choice with consequences, and a distinct way the story could develop. Change only those three files.
kb_delivery: Read notes/source.md and build exactly these three pages: kb/index.md (80-150 words), kb/state.md (120-220 words), and kb/questions.md (80-150 words), counting headings and link labels. The index must explain how to use the bible and link to both other pages with relative Markdown links. Each other page must link back to the index and across to its sibling. All links must resolve. Keep the whole KB within 520 words. Put settled facts and clearly attributed claims on the state page, and uncertainties or possible branches on the questions page. Change only these three KB files; leave source notes alone. These pages are the deliverable, not a prose scene or a promise to create them.
continuity: Preserve the supplied facts and their limits of knowledge. A suspicion, proposal, or missing result must not quietly become established truth. New dialogue and physical detail are welcome when they do not settle an open factual question.
explicit: Use third-person past tense. For a scene, remain close to the first named character and end on a concrete choice or action rather than an explanation of the theme. For alternatives or a bible, keep narration plain and label established facts separately from possibilities.
loose: You can choose the viewpoint, balance of dialogue, and shape of the ending. I want something I can work with, rather than a comprehensive account of the world.
permits_reply: You may choose reversible creative details without asking. Briefly name a consequential working assumption before the prose; that note counts toward the reply's word limit. If we revise later, the final version can simply give the prose once that assumption is settled.
permits_file: You may choose reversible creative details without asking. Briefly tell me any consequential working assumption in your reply, keeping the deliverable files focused on their requested content.
must_not: Please proceed without asking questions. The supplied facts are binding; use your own judgment for the remaining creative choices.
deep: We will work through several passes. Keep earlier author decisions unless I explicitly replace them; later messages refine this same deliverable and retain its paths and word budgets. On the last pass, deliver every requested artifact in full.
f5_intro: The current rule for {code} is in the project records. Use search to locate it, then read the matching record and its status context. The workspace includes withdrawn versions and irrelevant documents; do not assume the first match is authoritative. The index describes the authority convention. Quote the complete sentence under Current instruction verbatim once within the scene so its effect on the characters is clear. Do not quote the superseded instruction. Do not edit any project file.

rubric_anchors.1: Misses the purpose or contradicts supplied decisions.
rubric_anchors.3: Usable, but some choices are generic or constraints weakly integrated.
rubric_anchors.4: Effective and grounded, with minor weaknesses.
rubric_anchors.5: Specific, coherent, and faithful to the author's decisions throughout.
